annotation.authors_or_issuer: U.S. Coast Guard, Department of Homeland Security
annotation.summary_en: This is the US Coast Guard's federal regulation on maritime security (33 CFR Part 101). It puts the Maritime Transportation Security Act and the international SOLAS/ISPS rules into effect. It covers threat levels (MARSEC), security directives, enforcement, worker identity credentials (TWIC) and, since 2025, minimum cybersecurity requirements for US-flagged vessels and facilities. It does not deal with AI or robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Sets three maritime security threat levels (MARSEC Levels 1–3). The Coast Guard Commandant raises or lowers the level according to risk.
Requires suspicious activity, security breaches and transportation security incidents to be reported to the National Response Center.
Requires anyone needing unescorted access to secure areas to hold a worker identity credential (TWIC), with electronic checks for the highest-risk group (Risk Group A).
Subpart F (2025) requires a Cybersecurity Officer, a Coast Guard-approved Cybersecurity Plan, annual audits, drills and penetration testing.

Sets minimum cyber controls, including multifactor authentication, separating IT and operational-technology networks, patching known exploited vulnerabilities, staff training and reporting cyber incidents.
